 1 passenger remains hospitalized after Mississippi River tanker crash 
 The Atlantic Asphalt tanker collided with the American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage on Nov. 13, 2026 at 12:30 p.m. on the Mississippi River at the Port of New Orleans. (WVUE) By Judy Black Published : Nov. 20, 2026 at 7:26 AM CST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - New Orleans officials said only one passenger remains hospitalized after the Nov. 13 tanker crash into the cruise ship American Heritage.
 On Friday (Nov. 20), New Orleans officials said the only person hospitalized is in serious condition, with the three other passengers reported hospitalized just prior to Friday having since been released.
 The Port of New Orleans press secretary said the Atlantic Asphalt tanker crashed into the American Heritage around 12:30 p.m. on Nov. 13.
 Officials said all passengers were accounted for and 32 people were initially sent to hospitals.

 The aftermath
 The American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage sits on its side in the Mississippi River in front of the Port NOLA offices after a tanker crashed into the docked river cruiser. 
 Efforts to salvage the American Heritage have shifted underwater as the river cruise ship lies on its side. The immediate goal is to offload thousands of gallons of fuel, but it’s no easy task.
 Before salvage operations can begin, the Coast Guard is supervising the fuel offload.
 Dive flags now float alongside the American Heritage, marking the first phase of salvage operations.
 “Getting the fuel off is really important,” said Lt. Cmdr. Rachel Ault with the U.S. Coast Guard.
 Ault said crews must extract 16,000 gallons of fuel through a process called hot tapping. Divers will place a line inside the tanks to have the fuel pumped out.
 The Coast Guard said it could take a week to remove all the fuel and begin salvage operations. The NTSB is investigating the cause and said it could issue a preliminary report in 30 days.
